Prepared for Negs from the manufacturer's datasheet: FUJIFILM Professional Film Data Guide (US), Ref. No. AF3-207U, (c) 2005 Fuji Photo Film Co., Ltd., PDF page 27 (spectral sensitivity, per-dye spectral density, characteristic curves; RMS granularity 10). PDF sha256 64c6455651b9f13f5cd190219e4928d1fdf13ecf33859c4691d830bced8d3d36. Data (c) FUJIFILM Corporation. The curves were read from the PDF's vector paths (tools/film_profiles/extract_pdf.py); the points and axis calibration are in data/profile-sources/fujifilm-reversal/fujifilm_64t_type_ii/.
Method: spektrafilm's public-era profile creator by Andrea Volpato (commit b2c7fe6), its steps for positive films: D-min removed (base synthesised from the curves' D-min), log E zero where green is 0.735 over D-min, Fujifilm's own per-dye spectra scaled so equal amounts view as an 18.4 % neutral under the viewing illuminant, status-A unmixing, a 3 norm_cdfs curve fit, sensitivity balance, densitometer normalisation. Then Negs's steps: sensitivity scaled so an 18.4 % grey gives raw exposure 1 per channel under the reference illuminant, each channel aligned so log E 0 develops its metameric-neutral amount, and spektrafilm's slide grey-ramp refinement run on spektrafilm 28bf883 at data_trustability 1.0. hanatos2025 adaptation window [431.2, 17.8, 600.3, 44.9] fitted on the reflectance corpus (Otsu (https://github.com/enneract/otsu2018), Munsell (https://zenodo.org/records/3269912), human skin (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/reflectance-measurements-human-skin), forest colors (https://zenodo.org/records/3269920)) with a weak prior toward the median of spektrafilm's stored windows. Tools and procedure: tools/film_profiles, docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11.
Negs slide neutralisation (tools/film_profiles/neutralise_positive.py, a Negs step, not spektrafilm's): the red and blue curve models are moved so a grey card filmed at EV -3 to +2.5 and scanned stays neutral, while the status-A densities stay within about 0.10 D (or their deviation before the step, if larger; a soft limit) of the datasheet's characteristic curves, the curves change as little as possible and the DIR pre-correction does not fold; green is not touched. Weights tuned on Provia 100F and tested on Velvia 100, Ektachrome 100 and Kodachrome 64 (data/profile-sources/fujifilm-reversal/calibration/neutralisation_test.json). For this film: grey-ramp neutrality (EV -1 to +2) 0.0189 before, 0.0026 after; largest colour of the ramp C*ab 1.68 before, 0.80 after; largest curve change 0.053 D; worst status-A deviation from the datasheet 0.102 D (before 0.080 D).
Negs choices: reference illuminant BB3100, a 3100 K blackbody (tungsten stock exposed at 3100 K); viewing illuminant D50; no target print (a slide is viewed or scanned); log_sensitivity_density_over_min 1.0 as printed; spectra left empty (null) outside the published wavelength range; characteristic curves in log10 H as printed; use 'still' and antihalation 'strong' as the shipped spektrafilm Velvia 100 and Provia 100F; DIR couplers: the class default for colour slides.
Note: Reference illuminant BB3100, a 3100 K blackbody, as the datasheet's 'Tungsten (3100K)'. Slides have no tungsten coupler branch, so the cine 'T' convention does not apply.
Recorded extraction exceptions: sensitivity x axis, gate 0.4 % of span: Hand-drafted chart (Professional Film Data Guide; plot about 95 x 85 pt, characteristic curves 140 x 113 pt) whose own gridlines are unevenly spaced by up to 1.6 pt, so no straight axis reproduces them within 0.2 %. Worst gridline 0.31 % of the span (1.05 nm); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. The error is bounded by the calibration against spektrafilm's own digitisations of Provia 100F and Velvia 100 and by the charts the guide repeats for other films (docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11). dye_density y axis, gate 0.7 % of span: Only two gridlines (1.0, 0.5) are drawn; 0.0 is printed at the plot's bottom edge, which is taken as the zero tick. It sits 1.58 pt from where the gridlines' spacing alone would put 0.0; with that zero the lowest dye value would be -0.013 D (a dye density cannot be negative). Worst position 0.63 % of the span (0.009 D); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. Only the zero matters: the dye scale is renormalised later (densitometer normalisation). See docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11. characteristic x axis, gate 0.3 % of span: Hand-drafted chart (Professional Film Data Guide; plot about 95 x 85 pt, characteristic curves 140 x 113 pt) whose own gridlines are unevenly spaced by up to 1.6 pt, so no straight axis reproduces them within 0.2 %. Worst gridline 0.21 % of the span (0.0107 log H); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. The error is bounded by the calibration against spektrafilm's own digitisations of Provia 100F and Velvia 100 and by the charts the guide repeats for other films (docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11).

Prepared for Negs from the manufacturer's datasheet: FUJIFILM Professional Film Data Guide (US), Ref. No. AF3-207U, (c) 2005 Fuji Photo Film Co., Ltd., PDF page 26 (spectral sensitivity, per-dye spectral density, characteristic curves; RMS granularity 13). PDF sha256 64c6455651b9f13f5cd190219e4928d1fdf13ecf33859c4691d830bced8d3d36. Data (c) FUJIFILM Corporation. The curves were read from the PDF's vector paths (tools/film_profiles/extract_pdf.py); the points and axis calibration are in data/profile-sources/fujifilm-reversal/fujifilm_provia_400f/.
Method: spektrafilm's public-era profile creator by Andrea Volpato (commit b2c7fe6), its steps for positive films: D-min removed (base synthesised from the curves' D-min), log E zero where green is 0.735 over D-min, Fujifilm's own per-dye spectra scaled so equal amounts view as an 18.4 % neutral under the viewing illuminant, status-A unmixing, a 3 norm_cdfs curve fit, sensitivity balance, densitometer normalisation. Then Negs's steps: sensitivity scaled so an 18.4 % grey gives raw exposure 1 per channel under the reference illuminant, each channel aligned so log E 0 develops its metameric-neutral amount, and spektrafilm's slide grey-ramp refinement run on spektrafilm 28bf883 at data_trustability 1.0. hanatos2025 adaptation window [419.0, 28.8, 596.1, 40.4] fitted on the reflectance corpus (Otsu (https://github.com/enneract/otsu2018), Munsell (https://zenodo.org/records/3269912), human skin (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/reflectance-measurements-human-skin), forest colors (https://zenodo.org/records/3269920)) with a weak prior toward the median of spektrafilm's stored windows. Tools and procedure: tools/film_profiles, docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11.
Negs slide neutralisation (tools/film_profiles/neutralise_positive.py, a Negs step, not spektrafilm's): the red and blue curve models are moved so a grey card filmed at EV -3 to +2.5 and scanned stays neutral, while the status-A densities stay within about 0.10 D (or their deviation before the step, if larger; a soft limit) of the datasheet's characteristic curves, the curves change as little as possible and the DIR pre-correction does not fold; green is not touched. Weights tuned on Provia 100F and tested on Velvia 100, Ektachrome 100 and Kodachrome 64 (data/profile-sources/fujifilm-reversal/calibration/neutralisation_test.json). For this film: grey-ramp neutrality (EV -1 to +2) 0.0140 before, 0.0004 after; largest colour of the ramp C*ab 1.01 before, 0.04 after; largest curve change 0.033 D; worst status-A deviation from the datasheet 0.100 D (before 0.095 D).

Worst gridline 0.33 % of the span (1.12 nm); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. The error is bounded by the calibration against spektrafilm's own digitisations of Provia 100F and Velvia 100 and by the charts the guide repeats for other films (docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11). dye_density y axis, gate 1.1 % of span: Only two gridlines (1.0, 0.5) are drawn; 0.0 is printed at the plot's bottom edge, which is taken as the zero tick. It sits 2.58 pt from where the gridlines' spacing alone would put 0.0; with that zero the lowest dye value would be -0.024 D (a dye density cannot be negative). Worst position 1.03 % of the span (0.013 D); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. Only the zero matters: the dye scale is renormalised later (densitometer normalisation). See docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11. characteristic x axis, gate 0.4 % of span: Hand-drafted chart (Professional Film Data Guide; plot about 95 x 85 pt, characteristic curves 140 x 113 pt) whose own gridlines are unevenly spaced by up to 1.6 pt, so no straight axis reproduces them within 0.2 %. Worst gridline 0.32 % of the span (0.0159 log H); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. The error is bounded by the calibration against spektrafilm's own digitisations of Provia 100F and Velvia 100 and by the charts the guide repeats for other films (docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11). characteristic y axis, gate 0.5 % of span: Hand-drafted chart (Professional Film Data Guide; plot about 95 x 85 pt, characteristic curves 140 x 113 pt) whose own gridlines are unevenly spaced by up to 1.6 pt, so no straight axis reproduces them within 0.2 %. Worst gridline 0.49 % of the span (0.0199 D); gate rounded up to the next 0.1 %. The error is bounded by the calibration against spektrafilm's own digitisations of Provia 100F and Velvia 100 and by the charts the guide repeats for other films (docs/adding-film-stocks.md D11).

Prepared for Negs from the manufacturer's datasheet: FUJICOLOR REALA ACE data sheet (Japanese), Ref. No. 013Ai158A, 1996 (layout stamp 96.3-HB), PDF page 4 (spectral sensitivity, characteristic curves, minimum and midscale-neutral spectral density; RMS granularity 4). PDF sha256 04bb3116657b2263aa19682ff56cb41c779ed14931272325d42e9f753b64b918. Data (c) FUJIFILM Corporation. The curves were read from the PDF's vector paths (tools/film_profiles/extract_pdf.py); the points and axis calibration are in data/profile-sources/fujifilm-jp/fujifilm_reala_ace/.
Method: spektrafilm's public-era profile creator by Andrea Volpato (commit b2c7fe6), steps 1-8: D-min removed, log E zero where green is 0.2 over D-min plus 3 stops, dye spectra reconstructed (dmid_dmin) from spektrafilm's generic_a dye set (Giorgianni, Madden & Kriss 2009, p. 112, via spektrafilm) because the datasheet gives no per-dye spectra, status-M unmixing, a 3 norm_cdfs curve fit, sensitivity balance, midscale alignment 'green' (of none/green/mid, the lowest grey-ramp neutrality error, none 0.088, green 0.076, mid 0.078, among those whose fujifilm_crystal_archive_typeii neutral filters fall in the shipped films' range), densitometer normalisation. Then Negs's steps: sensitivity scaled so an 18.4 % grey gives raw exposure 1 per channel under the reference illuminant, and spektrafilm's grey-ramp refinement run on spektrafilm 28bf883 through fujifilm_crystal_archive_typeii at data_trustability 0.3. hanatos2025 adaptation window [397.8, 21.8, 616.5, 61.3] fitted on the reflectance corpus (Otsu (https://github.com/enneract/otsu2018), Munsell (https://zenodo.org/records/3269912), human skin (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/reflectance-measurements-human-skin), forest colors (https://zenodo.org/records/3269920)) with a weak prior toward the median of spektrafilm's stored windows. Tools and procedure: tools/film_profiles, docs/adding-film-stocks.md.
Negs choices: reference illuminant D55 (daylight stock, exposed at 5400 K); viewing illuminant D50; target print fujifilm_crystal_archive_typeii; log_sensitivity_density_over_min 1.0 as printed; spectra left empty (null) outside the published wavelength range; characteristic curves in log10 H as printed; use 'still' and antihalation 'weak' as the shipped Fujifilm still negatives (C200, X-TRA 400, Superia 200, Reala 100, Pro 160NS).
Note: the datasheet's dashed fourth colour layer (第4の感色層, cyan-sensitive) is not modelled: the three-layer model takes the blue, green and red sensitive layers only
Recorded validation exception: the reconstructed dyes reproduce D-mid minus D-min within 0.043 D (worst at 585 nm), over the 0.03 D criterion; the §D3 fallback (a flat extension past 700 nm) was not tried, as the worst point is not near 700 nm. Weighted per fujifilm_crystal_archive_typeii print channel the residual is R/G/B +0.0016, +0.0039, +0.0085 D, within the 0.01 D the method accepts for this case (approved by Noah 2026-11-14).
Relative axes: sensitivity y axis: Relative sensitivity (log), no tick values: a 1.0 scale bar spans the two gridlines (one log unit). The offset is arbitrary; D5 rescales every channel so it does not reach the profile.
Recorded extraction exceptions: characteristic y axis, gate 0.3 % of span: hand-drafted grid reused across Fujifilm Japan's data sheets (Venus 800 and Natura 1600 share the dye chart's residuals to 0.001 %): no straight axis reproduces the gridlines within 0.2 % (worst 0.23 %, 0.009 D). The extraction error is bounded by that residual whether the curves were drawn to the true scale or to the drawn grid. Physical check: Natura 1600 from these sheets against the independent Professional Film Data Guide AF3-207U trace of the same emulsion (Superia 1600): curves within 0.009 D, spectra within 0.021 D (README, calibration/natura_1600_vs_pfdg_superia_1600_curves.json, calibration/vs_pfdg_all_panels.json).

Prepared for Negs from the manufacturer's datasheet: EASTMAN EXR 100T Color Negative Film 5248/7248, Technical Data / Color Negative Film, KODAK Publication No. H-1-7248, March 1999 (©Eastman Kodak Company, 1999; Minor Revision 3-99), PDF page 3 (spectral sensitivity, characteristic curves, minimum and midscale-neutral spectral density; RMS granularity less than 5). PDF sha256 4735518c66d406e508928715f932a626b9f1e23647d45fd84f8c3cd4133291fc. Data (c) Eastman Kodak Company. The curves were read from the PDF's vector paths (tools/film_profiles/extract_pdf.py); the points and axis calibration are in data/profile-sources/kodak-cine/kodak_exr_100t/.
Method: spektrafilm's public-era profile creator by Andrea Volpato (commit b2c7fe6), steps 1-8: D-min removed, log E zero where green is 0.2 over D-min plus 3 stops, dye spectra reconstructed (dmid_dmin) from spektrafilm's generic_a dye set (Giorgianni, Madden & Kriss 2009, p. 112, via spektrafilm) because the datasheet gives no per-dye spectra, status-M unmixing, a 3 norm_cdfs curve fit, sensitivity balance, midscale alignment 'mid' (of none/green/mid, the lowest grey-ramp neutrality error, none 0.085, green 0.058, mid 0.049, among those whose kodak_2383 neutral filters fall in the shipped films' range), densitometer normalisation. Then Negs's steps: sensitivity scaled so an 18.4 % grey gives raw exposure 1 per channel under the reference illuminant, and spektrafilm's grey-ramp refinement run on spektrafilm 28bf883 through kodak_2383 at data_trustability 0.3. hanatos2025 adaptation window [394.4, 21.5, 610.4, 59.2] fitted on the reflectance corpus (Otsu (https://github.com/enneract/otsu2018), Munsell (https://zenodo.org/records/3269912), human skin (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/reflectance-measurements-human-skin), forest colors (https://zenodo.org/records/3269920)) with a weak prior toward the median of spektrafilm's stored windows. Tools and procedure: tools/film_profiles, docs/adding-film-stocks.md.
Negs choices: reference illuminant T, colour-science's incandescent SPD, as Kodak's tungsten Vision3 profiles (tungsten stock, exposed at 3200 K); viewing illuminant D50; target print kodak_2383; log_sensitivity_density_over_min 0.4 as printed; spectra left empty (null) outside the published wavelength range; characteristic curves in log10 H as printed (the chart's log lux-seconds scale); use 'cine' and antihalation 'strong' as the Vision3 and Eterna profiles.
Window prior weight 0.003 instead of 0.002: at the default 0.002 the fit put c_uv at 389.1 nm, under the shipped windows' range (391-456; D8 check 10); 0.003 is the smallest of 0.003/0.004/0.006/0.01 that passes, giving [394.4, 21.5, 610.4, 59.2] at a corpus loss 2 % above the unconstrained fit (0.0215 against 0.0211; no window 0.0276).
Note: The characteristic chart has two exposure scales: log lux-seconds on top (ticks 3-bar.0 to 1.0, labelled at both frame edges) and camera stops below. They disagree by 9 % (one drawn stop is 0.276 log10 H on the top scale, not 0.301). The curves are read on the top scale, the sensitometric one, which gives a green mid-scale gamma of about 0.59; the stop scale would give about 0.54.

Then the author's print normalisation (spektrafilm #557): sensitivities scaled so the TH-KG3 enlarger lamp through Y50 M50 and the mid-scale neutral of kodak_vision3_250d gives raw exposure 1 per channel. Negs step before the unmixing: each status-A curve moved along log E so log E 0 develops the metameric neutral's status-A density (the private creator's preliminary neutral shift; R +0.165, G -0.033, B +0.074 log E). Calibration: the same steps rebuild Kodak 2383 and 2393 from spektrafilm's public raw data to within CIEDE2000 0.9-1.0 mean (2.6 at most) of the shipped profiles on a ColorChecker printed from cine negatives, and their neutral filters within about 3 CC (data/profile-sources/fujifilm-print/calibration/). Tools and procedure: tools/film_profiles, docs/adding-film-stocks.md D12.
Brochure specifics: the characteristic curves' log H axis is unlabelled (one square is 0.5 log H), and green and blue are plotted 1.0 and 2.0 log H to the left of red; the shift is undone, and the pre-alignment fixes each channel's position anyway. Fujifilm draws each dye curve with the film base under it (where all four are drawn, Y + M + C - Gray = 2 x base). The base taken off is the one this brochure's own dye chart implies, smoothed 20 nm. Undrawn parts filled: yellow 685-695 nm from the Gray curve less the other two dyes and the base. Sensitivity is drawn only near each peak (red in two pieces, 360-442 nm and 630-723 nm): beyond each drawn end it continues with the shape of kodak_2383 (Kodak's ECP-2 print film, the calibration stock), joined at the end and only falling away from it. Share of the normalisation's raw exposure from these tails: R 12%, G 1%, B 0% (red: mostly 600-640 nm, where an orange-masked negative passes the most light).

Printed as 2854K tungsten, 1/100 s, Fuji SC-41 + CC-90Y + CC-60M; ECP-2B.
Recorded exceptions: characteristic x axis (relative): Exposure [log H] carries no numbers, only a 0.5 log H scale bar spanning one grid square; the offset is arbitrary (log E 0 is set by step 2 and the neutral pre-alignment) and the scale is 0.5 log H per square.
